Fold-internal residualization (the UMFI-LR preprocessing)

Source: R/residualize.R
residualize_fit.Rd

residualize_fit() regresses every column of x except the anchor on the anchor by ordinary least squares with an intercept and returns the coefficients. residualize_apply() applies previously estimated coefficients to (possibly different) rows, so that assessment data can be transformed with coefficients estimated on training data only. build_representations() combines the two to produce the full and reduced representations used by shared_importance().

Usage

residualize_fit(x, anchor)

residualize_apply(x, coefs)

build_representations(x_train, x_assess, anchor)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) with column names. For residualize_fit() these are the training rows.

anchor

Column name or index of the anchor feature.

coefs

An object returned by residualize_fit().

x_train, x_assess

Training and assessment rows with identical columns.

Value

residualize_fit() returns a list of class sharedimp_residualization with elements anchor (column name), features (names of the other columns, in their original order), intercept and slope (named numeric vectors, one entry per other column), collinear (named logical vector, TRUE for columns whose residual is fixed at zero), constant_anchor (logical) and n_train.

residualize_apply() returns a numeric matrix with one column per entry of coefs$features, in that order.

build_representations() returns a list with full_train, full_assess (all p columns in the original order, the anchor raw and in its original position, the others residualized), reduced_train, reduced_assess (the same without the anchor column) and coefs.

Details

For anchor i and every other column j, b_j = Cov(x_i, x_j) / Var(x_i) and a_j = mean(x_j) - b_j * mean(x_i), both computed on the rows passed to residualize_fit(). The residualized column is x_j - a_j - b_j * x_i.

Two deterministic rules cover degenerate cases (specification Section 5.1):

  • If the anchor has zero sum of squares about its mean on the fitting rows (it is constant), all slopes are set to zero, the intercepts become the column means, and a warning of class sharedimp_constant_anchor is raised.

  • If a column j is (numerically) an exact affine function of the anchor on the fitting rows, i.e. its residual sum of squares is at most 1e-10 times its total sum of squares, it is flagged in collinear and its residual is set to exactly 0 in residualize_apply(), for fitting and new rows alike. The column is kept, so the representations always have p and p - 1 columns.

No noise is ever injected and no column is ever dropped.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- cbind(a = rnorm(20), b = rnorm(20), c = rnorm(20))
x[, "b"] <- 2 * x[, "a"] + x[, "b"]
cf <- residualize_fit(x[1:15, ], anchor = "b")
cf$slope
#>         a         c 
#> 0.4696116 0.1309606 
r <- residualize_apply(x[16:20, ], cf)
rep <- build_representations(x[1:15, ], x[16:20, ], anchor = "b")
colnames(rep$full_train) # anchor "b" stays in the second position
#> [1] "a" "b" "c"
colnames(rep$reduced_train)
#> [1] "a" "c"
